title: Composite index for org-scoped IN+GROUP BY lookups
answers: Service account token count search is slow under concurrency
Query with WHERE org_id = ? AND x IN (...) GROUP BY x scans too much
Why add a composite index instead of relying on existing single-column indexes?
Does the service-account secret scanner query benefit from this index too?
body: Symptom: service-account search's token-count query (WHERE org_id = ? AND service_account_id IN (...) GROUP BY service_account_id) scans the whole organization's api_key rows, and this amplifies under concurrent searches on large installs. Root cause: no index existed covering both org_id and service_account_id together (pkg/services/sqlstore/migrations/apikey_mig.go). Fix pattern: add a nonunique composite index on the exact (filter-col, filter-col) pair used together in WHERE+GROUP BY, via NewAddIndexMigration — on MySQL/InnoDB this also covers COUNT(id) queries since secondary indexes include the primary key. Constraints: this only helps queries filtering/grouping by exactly org_id+service_account_id together; it does not speed up the secret scanner's separate global name-sort query, which is unaffected and unchanged.
applies: Query-performance fixes for api_key/service-account token lookups and similar org-scoped multi-column filters
says: Service account token count search is slow under heavy concurrent load
Why does the service account search query perform poorly on large instances
Service account lookup becomes sluggish with many simultaneous search requests
Slow performance when filtering or counting service account tokens
search: Service-account token-count queries filtering by WHERE org_id = ? AND service_account_id IN (...) GROUP BY service_account_id require a nonunique composite index on (org_id, service_account_id) to avoid scanning entire organization rows, especially under concurrent load. Add the index via NewAddIndexMigration in pkg/services/sqlstore/migrations/apikey_mig.go; on MySQL/InnoDB, secondary indexes include the primary key so this also covers COUNT(id). This optimization applies only to queries that filter and group by exactly this column pair together; it does not affect separate unrelated queries like global name-sort lookups.
